title: Edge enforcer window drift during DST switch causes brief unmetered bursts
creator: Asha Patel
description:
Summary: On 2025-11-02 we observed a customer report of a short period (~3–7 minutes) of unmetered requests immediately after a Daylight Saving Time (DST) forward clock change in a specific cloud region. Investigation shows edge-level rate enforcers momentarily accepted traffic exceeding per-key and per-route quotas without backfilling debits. This ticket tracks diagnosis and remediation for the DST/clock-drift interaction with our sliding-window policy engine.

Reproduction steps (observed):
1) Edge proxies receive requests from clients at real time T (local TZ DST transition).
2) Edge enforcer computes policy window boundaries based on local system time rather than monotonic epoch.
3) During the forward jump, the window end timestamp briefly appears earlier than the last debit epoch, causing the enforcer to treat incoming requests as belonging to the new window with zeroed counters.
4) Requests are allowed; central aggregator receives delayed deltas and does not reconcile or retroactively debit because the enforcer did not emit appropriate overflow events.

Scope & Impact:
- Affected surface: per-key and per-route sliding-window enforcers on edge nodes in regions with DST transitions (primary impact seen in eu-west-2 staging and us-east-2 test fleets).
- Customer impact: potential short-term overuse without throttling or billing debits; observed customers had small token overages but this could scale to high-volume tenants.
- Severity: High for billing correctness and customer trust; low immediate safety risk for runtime but unacceptable accounting drift.

Evidence & Artifacts:
- Logs: /var/log/enforcer/edge-2025-11-02.log (attached to incident ticket) shows window_end values jumping backward at 02:00 local time.
- Trace: TraceID 9f3a2c7b shows request sequence allowed despite quota exhaustion at T+30s.
- Metrics: meter_delta_delays and window_boundary_skew grafana panels spike at the same timestamp.
- Repro harness: small script in repo infra/tests/enforcer_time_skew that simulates clock jumps.

Hypothesis:
- Root cause appears to be reliance on wall-clock time to compute sliding-window buckets on edge enforcers. When system time jumps forward (or experiences any negative perceived delta), the algorithm resets or advances bucket pointers incorrectly. The central aggregator assumes monotonic bucket progression and ignores late/duplicate messages, leading to net undercharging.

Short-term mitigations implemented (rolled to canary on eu-west-2 edges 2025-11-04):
- Patch enforcer to use monotonic clock (CLOCK_MONOTONIC) for internal window progression and only translate to wall time for logs/metrics.
- Add a safety guard: if a received request would cause allowed_count > burst_threshold and local monotonic delta indicates a backwards jump, throttle to burst_threshold until reconciled.
- Start a backfill job that consumes the delayed deltas and emits synthetic debit events to central billing for the observed window where over-allowance occurred (disabled for PII customers).

Long-term fixes proposed:
- Migrate all edge enforcers to monotonic-based epoch counters and make RPC payloads include epoch IDs and monotonic offsets.
- Enhance central aggregator to accept out-of-order deltas and perform idempotent backfill reconciliation with TTL-limited retro-debits and compensating metrics.
- Add a testing gate in CI that simulates time jumps for every release touching rate-limiter code.

Open questions:
- Do we need to retroactively bill customers for historical events? (Finance/Legal input required.)
- Should we expand the fallback to forcibly reject traffic for any region that experiences clock anomalies, or prefer graceful throttling?

Next steps:
1) Complete code review for monotonic-clock patch (PR #7428).
2) Run an extended canary (72h) in two regions and validate no meter drift.
3) Coordinate with Finance on customer notification / compensation policy if we detect >1000 token overages per org during transitions.
4) Add time-jump CI tests and document explicit requirements for edge OS NTP configs.

Related artifacts: PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/7428, repro script: https://github.com/redwood-inference/infra/tree/main/tests/enforcer_time_skew, dashboard: https://grafana.redwood-internal.com/d/abc123/window-skew-overview
